text:
marta: Quick thread — I updated the Q3 GPU-hour forecast and we need to decide on packing policy before the summer burst. TL;DR: projected +34% GPU hours in July-Aug vs baseline and our current fragmentation numbers will blow cost targets.

jamal: link to the sheet?

marta: https://internal.redwood/forecasts/q3-gpu-hours — key row is 'high-traffic-playground' which drives most of the delta.

alec: numbers? rough ballpark is easier for planning.

marta: baseline 310k GPU hours/mo -> spike scenario 417k GPU hours/mo (35% increase). Peak daily GPU-hours 52k.

sophia: Oof. That'll hit us on both Hosted and Dedicated burst pools. Any regional skew?

marta: yes — 60% APAC-eu mix shift: APAC regions see 2x growth vs NA in the spike window.

kenji: Our current bin-packing policy is "balanced-first" which spreads tenants to avoid noisy neighbors. That increases fragmentation for many small jobs.

jamal: We have two knobs: aggressive pack (pack-small-first + tolerate co-tenancy) or bucketized SLAs (pin high-sla to isolated nodes). Tradeoffs?

alec: Aggressive pack reduces fragmentation but increases tail latency risk for latency-sensitive tenants. Bucketized SLAs increase capacity overhead (reserve nodes) but protect P99.

sophia: How much fragmentation are we seeing now? Metric from the runtime?

kenji: From last week's snapshot: average free-gpu per-node = 0.74, average utilization = 64%, fragmentation metric (sum unallocable vram) normalized = 0.18. Predictive sim says tighter packing can cut fragmentation to 0.06.

marta: Sim results: tight-pack policy -> -18% total GPU hours, but P99 latency for small chat bursts increases 120ms on avg. Bucketized -> +9% reserved hours but P99 stable.

jamal: Cost calc?

marta: Rough estimate: at current unit costs, -18% GPU hours -> ~$210k/month saved during spike months. Bucketized approach -> adds ~$85k/month.

alec: Can we mix? e.g., pack best-effort and batch-y workloads aggressively, keep low-latency customers on dedicated SLA buckets.

kenji: We already have a label system. Proposal: label tenants with `sla:latency|best-effort|throughput`. Scheduler rule: pack `best-effort` onto spot-capacity and nodes with >1 job slot; keep `latency` on 1-job-per-gpu nodes. Also allow regional bursting: allow best-effort to burst into APAC overflow nodes.

sophia: How do we implement regional bursting safely? Network egress and data locality will bite. Also contractual concerns for enterprise customers pinned to region.

marta: Agreed. We can add a policy: cross-region-burst allowed only for tenants with opt-in flag and non-sensitive data. Default enterprise flagged `geo_lock: true` to prevent cross-region.

jamal: Can we get an example scheduler config snippet to review?

kenji: paste below:
```yaml
scheduler:
  policies:
    - name: latency_bucket
      selector: "sla == 'latency'"
      max_co_tenants: 1
      region_lock: true
    - name: aggressive_pack
      selector: "sla == 'best-effort' or job_type == 'batch'"
      max_co_tenants: 8
      allow_cross_region_burst: true
      preemption: low
```

alec: That's sensible. What about eviction impacts? If we preempt many best-effort jobs in APAC, we could create large KV cache churns and regen overhead.

kenji: We should couple preemption with KV-cache-preserve hints and checkpointing for long-running fine-tuning jobs. Also limit cross-region burst to jobs < 4h.

sophia: Ops playbook? If P99 in Hosted crosses threshold we should automatically throttle aggressive_pack and shift to bucketized policy. Can we add an automated rollback?

marta: Yes — plan: automatic SLO-based rollback at P99 > SLA + 25ms for 10m window. SRE bot will post incident and flip policy.

sre-bot: [auto] Observability alert rule created: `gpu.p99_latency > sla_threshold + 25ms` -> runbook `binpack-rollover-v1`.

jamal: Do we need more capacity in Dedicated reserved pools to cover enterprise contracts?

marta: For Q3 we recommend +15% reserved commit in NA and +25% in APAC for July-Aug. This keeps contractual risk low and gives headroom.

alec: How about costing for that reserved commit vs relying on aggressive pack? Mix looks like: reserved commit + pack best-effort -> net +3% cost vs baseline but much lower SLA risk and simpler ops.

sophia: I like the hybrid. Action items?

marta: 1) Kenji to prototype scheduler policy and sim results by EOD Thu (1784615400). 2) Jamal to update forecasting sheet with bucketed vs aggressive scenarios and cost delta by Monday. 3) Alec to draft PRD for SLA bucket rollout and tenant opt-in UI.

kenji: On it. Will push a sim branch and link.

jamal: I'll annotate the top tenants that cause most fragmentation.

alec: I'll start the PRD skeleton.

sophia: I'll write the SLO rollback playbook and coordinate with legal on cross-region opt-in language.

marta: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after the sim results. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: [note] Thread pinned in #eng-infra for planning reference.
